---
title: "Glossary"
subtitle: "Alphabetical reference of TimeToAlign! model terminology"
---

This page collects all terms introduced in the [Conceptual Model](concepts.qmd).
Hover over any {{< glossary glossary >}}-highlighted term elsewhere on this site
to see its definition.

For the full context in which each term is introduced, follow the cross-references
to the relevant section of the conceptual model.


## A

**AlignmentAnchor**
:   A pure coordinate pair associating one coordinate on timeline A with one
    on timeline B. A neutral record with no claim semantics---provenance is
    carried by the enclosing {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}. Only synchronous
    MatchClaims produce AlignmentAnchors. From a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}
    of {{< glossary TimeIntervalEvent >}}s, one derives a **StartAnchor** and
    an **EndAnchor**.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**AlignmentBundle**
:   The top-level container for alignment workflows, holding timelines,
    {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}s, and cross-group
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s. Provides coordinate transfer within groups
    (via interpolation) and across groups (via {{< glossary MatchLine >}} and
    {{< glossary WarpMap >}}).
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

## B

**Break**
:   A {{< glossary ControlEvent >}} that voids {{< glossary Contiguity >}}
    at its {{< glossary Instant >}}. TimeIntervals cannot span a Break,
    and Breaks cannot be inserted into existing TimeIntervals.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

## C

**ChainMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} that applies multiple
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s in sequence, creating a conversion
    path from a source unit to a target unit.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Child**
:   A {{< glossary Timeline >}} nested within a parent timeline, sharing
    the same measuring unit. Children are locked upon insertion to prevent
    side effects from modifications.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**CombinationMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} yielding outputs from multiple
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s simultaneously (e.g., *(x, y)*
    coordinate pairs).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Commensurable**
:   Two timelines are commensurable when connected by a
    {{< glossary Match >}} path or {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} chain,
    enabling coordinate translation between them.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**ConcatenationMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} combining bounded
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s such that each coordinate region is
    handled by a specific map.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Contiguity**
:   A {{< glossary TimeInterval >}} is contiguous if it monotonically
    spans all coordinates between its start and end. An
    {{< glossary Instant >}} is contiguous with a TimeInterval if it is
    synchronous with its {{< glossary EndInstant >}}.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

**ControlEvent**
:   An event affecting flow control: either a {{< glossary Break >}}
    (voiding contiguity) or a {{< glossary Jump >}} (creating new
    contiguity).
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

**ConversionMap**
:   A function mapping any coordinate to at most one value (another
    coordinate, a specifier, or a constant). Also called **C-map**. If
    bijective, an {{< glossary InverseMap >}} can be derived.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Coordinate**
:   A position on a {{< glossary Timeline >}}, expressed as the distance
    from the origin in the timeline's measuring unit. Combines a numeric
    value with a TimeUnit.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## D

**DictStore**
:   A generic `EventStore` subclass holding a `dict[str, EventData]` with
    arbitrary keys. Used internally by AlignmentLoaders to store one
    `EventData` table per timeline-to-be (e.g., `"score"`, `"perf:p01"`).
    Maintains the uniform `EventStore` interface.
    See the [API reference](reference/timetoalign.DictStore.qmd).

**Discrete**
:   A timeline is discrete when coordinates exist only at discrete points
    (e.g., pixels, samples, ticks). Contrast with Continuous timelines
    where coordinates can take any real value (e.g., seconds, quarters).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Domain**
:   One of three temporal categories: **Graphical** (visual/spatial),
    **Logical** (symbolic/musical), or **Physical** (audio/sound). Each
    domain has both discrete and continuous timeline variants.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## E

**EndInstant**
:   An {{< glossary Instant >}} marking the end of a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}. Its coordinate must be greater than or
    equal to the corresponding {{< glossary StartInstant >}}'s coordinate.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Event**
:   Anything associated with a {{< glossary Timeline >}} via
    {{< glossary Instant >}}s. An {{< glossary InstantEvent >}} has zero
    duration; a {{< glossary TimeIntervalEvent >}} has duration defined by
    start and end coordinates.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## I

**Instant**
:   Associates a {{< glossary Coordinate >}} (a "time-point") with a
    signification such as "start of event *e*". Instants sharing a
    coordinate are synchronous.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**InstantEvent**
:   An {{< glossary Event >}} defined by a single {{< glossary Instant >}},
    having zero duration.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**InverseMap**
:   The reverse transformation of a bijective
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## J

**Jump**
:   A {{< glossary ControlEvent >}} with **JumpFrom** and **JumpTo**
    {{< glossary Instant >}}s. When active, makes events at JumpTo
    contiguous with those ending at JumpFrom (e.g., repeats, *dal segno*).
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

## L

**Length**
:   The distance between a {{< glossary Timeline >}}'s origin and its last
    {{< glossary Instant >}}.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Locked**
:   A timeline state preventing the addition of {{< glossary Instant >}}s
    after the last time-point. {{< glossary Child >}} timelines are
    automatically locked when embedded in a parent.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

## M

**Match**
:   See {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}. The manuscript shorthand "Match" refers
    to the MatchClaim concept.

**MatchfileLoader**
:   Loader for Vienna Match (`.match`) alignment files. Uses the standard
    two-phase `load()` → `create_*()` pattern. A single instance processes
    all `.match` files that share the same score, building a shared score
    timeline on the first file and verifying subsequent files against it.
    Returns an {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} directly via
    `create_alignment_bundle()`. Score goes into its own group; performances
    are standalone timelines; {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s connect score to
    performances.
    See the [API reference](reference/timetoalign.MatchfileLoader.qmd).

**MatchClaim**
:   A claim---issued by a human or algorithmic agent---about one or two timed
    things (events, regions, children) on two specific timelines. Always knows
    which pair of timelines it connects. Contains 0--2
    {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s (only if synchronous), synchrony and
    explicitness flags, and optional metadata (agent, decision criteria,
    certainty). Four cases: (a) event-to-event, (b) projection,
    (c) {{< glossary NOMATCH >}}, (d) implicit (from group extension).
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchGraph**
:   An on-demand analytical structure built from {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s
    using a networkx graph. Nodes are `(timeline_id, coordinate)` tuples;
    edges derive from {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s of synchronous claims.
    Connected components yield {{< glossary MatchStamp >}}s. Can be extended
    with implicit claims based on {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}} membership.
    Each Match box M1--M15 in the Hendrix figure is a MatchGraph.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchLine**
:   An ordered sequence of {{< glossary MatchStamp >}}s for a given source
    timeline, sorted by coordinate on that source timeline. Created by
    selecting and resolving {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s (all or a filtered
    subset). Used as input for {{< glossary WarpMap >}} generation.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchPath**
:   A path traversal connecting matched events across multiple timelines
    (e.g., A -> B -> C), enabling indirect alignment.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchStamp**
:   A synchronised instant across multiple timelines, extracted from a
    {{< glossary MatchGraph >}}'s connected components. Contains one
    coordinate per participating timeline. Can be expanded with
    group-member coordinates and C-map conversions.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MultiMap**
:   An umbrella term for composed {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s:
    {{< glossary ChainMap >}} (sequential),
    {{< glossary CombinationMap >}} (parallel outputs), and
    {{< glossary ConcatenationMap >}} (regional).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## N

**NOMATCH**
:   A sentinel value in a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} explicitly encoding the
    absence of a corresponding event on the other timeline. The MatchClaim
    records both timeline IDs but has no {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s;
    `is_synchronous` is always `False`.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

## O

**Origin**
:   The zero coordinate of a {{< glossary Timeline >}}, from which all
    positions are measured.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## P

**Parent**
:   A {{< glossary Timeline >}} that contains one or more
    {{< glossary Child >}} timelines. The parent and all its children must
    share the same measuring unit.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

## R

**raw_to_normalised**
:   The conventional name for the {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} (specifically
    a `ShiftMap`) attached to a score timeline to expose normalised
    (non-negative) coordinates. Its offset equals `−min(raw_onsets)`. Added
    by {{< glossary MatchfileLoader >}} and `PartituraLoader` so downstream
    code can detect and apply the same shift when comparing coordinates across
    loaders.

**Region**
:   A named part of a {{< glossary Timeline >}} defined by a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}} (e.g., "Chorus", "Verse"). Regions are
    not timelines and cannot hold events or maps directly.
    See [Regions](concepts.qmd#regions).

**Root**
:   The top-level {{< glossary Timeline >}} in a hierarchy of nested
    timelines. Only the root timeline can be extended; all descendants are
    locked.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**RotationMap**
:   A periodic {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} that wraps coordinates
    cyclically (e.g., an ostinato part that repeats while the main
    timeline advances).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## S

**Segment**
:   A {{< glossary Child >}} timeline that is contiguous with its
    siblings. Segments enable concatenation of local coordinate systems.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**SegmentLine**
:   A parent {{< glossary Timeline >}} containing only contiguous
    {{< glossary Segment >}}s. Enables cumulative coordinate conversion
    across all segments.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**StartInstant**
:   An {{< glossary Instant >}} marking the start of a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Synchrony**
:   *Strict synchrony*: {{< glossary Instant >}}s sharing identical
    coordinates. *Pragmatic synchrony*: Instants binned together based on
    a threshold (e.g., for quantisation).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## T

**TimeInterval**
:   Defined by a {{< glossary StartInstant >}} and
    {{< glossary EndInstant >}}; left-inclusive and right-exclusive
    [*s*, *e*). The EndInstant's coordinate must be >= the StartInstant's.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimeIntervalEvent**
:   An {{< glossary Event >}} with duration, defined by a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}. Contrast with
    {{< glossary InstantEvent >}}.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimeIntervalStamp**
:   Combination of a start {{< glossary TimeStamp >}} and an end
    TimeStamp, representing a cross-section of an interval through the
    timeline hierarchy.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**Timeline**
:   A positive coordinate axis minimally defined by its origin (zero) and
    measuring unit. Accommodates events and potentially
    {{< glossary Child >}} timelines.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimelineGroup**
:   A container for commensurable timelines, connected via a shared timestamp
    table and pairwise interpolation maps. Enables coordinate transfer between
    timelines of potentially different units via linear interpolation.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**TimeStamp**
:   A cross-section through a timeline hierarchy at a given coordinate.
    Computes equivalent coordinates on {{< glossary Child >}} timelines (via
    offset arithmetic) and on attached {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} target
    units.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**TraversalMap**
:   A sequence of {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}s representing a specific
    traversal path through a timeline (handling {{< glossary Jump >}}s and
    repeats). Also called **T-map**.
    See [Derivative timelines](concepts.qmd#derivative-timelines).

## W

**WarpMap**
:   A standalone class that produces a materialised copy of a source timeline
    (including its children, events, and regions), warped to the coordinate
    system of a target timeline. Generated from a {{< glossary MatchLine >}}
    by extracting coordinate pairs and building an interpolation table.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#coordinate-transfer).
